cards.name: Stone Cold Steve Austin, Texas Rattlesnake
cards.rules:
Trample
When Stone Cold Steve Austin enters the battlefield, create two Pop tokens.
Whenever a creature is dealt damage, gain 1 Momentum.
Whenever Stone Cold Steve Austin attacks, gain 2 Momentum.
As long as you have 10 or more Momentum, Stone Cold Steve Austin has indestructible and hexproof.
cards.flavor: "_And that's the bottom line, 'cause Stone Cold said so!_"
cards.art: bald defiant brawler in black vest and denim shorts, middle fingers raised, beer foam flying, roaring late-90s arena crowd, Attitude Era WWF

cards.name: Stone Cold Stunner
cards.rules:
As an additional cost to cast this spell, remove 10 Momentum.
Destroy target creature. You gain Momentum equal to half its power, rounded down.
cards.art: bald brawler in black vest delivering a jaw-jarring kick to a stunned opponent in a packed 1998 arena, beer cups flying, ringside flash photography, Attitude Era WWF

cards.name: Al Snow, Head Hunter
cards.rules: When Al Snow enters the battlefield, create a Pop token.
cards.art: eccentric wrestler carrying a mannequin head to the ring, roaring crowd chanting along, late-90s WWF arena

cards.name: Matt Hardy, The Anchor
cards.rules:
Haste
Tag team with Jeff Hardy, Daredevil *(At the beginning of your upkeep, if you control both members of one or more tag teams, create a Pop token. Only one token is created this way per turn.)*
cards.art: determined high-flyer in Hardy Boyz gear poised on the turnbuckle, roaring late-90s WWF crowd, 1999

cards.name: Jeff Hardy, Daredevil
cards.rules:
First strike
Tag team with Matt Hardy, The Anchor *(At the beginning of your upkeep, if you control both members of one or more tag teams, create a Pop token. Only one token is created this way per turn.)*
cards.art: daredevil with neon-dyed hair hitting a Swanton Bomb off a ladder, explosive crowd reaction, 1999 WWF arena

cards.name: Sable, Bombshell
cards.rules:
When Sable enters the battlefield, create two Pop tokens.
At the beginning of your upkeep, create a Pop token.
cards.flavor: "_Look at the puppies!_ — Jerry 'The King' Lawler"
cards.art: glamorous superstar making a show-stopping entrance down the ramp, flashbulbs exploding, roaring 1998 WWF crowd

cards.name: Mankind, The Deranged
cards.rules: When Mankind dies, create two Pop tokens.
cards.art: masked brawler slumped in the corner of the ring after taking a brutal beating, crowd on its feet roaring in sympathy, 1998 WWF arena

cards.name: The Kickout
cards.rules:
The first time a source deals damage to you each turn, create a Pop token.
The second time a source deals damage to you each turn, create two Pop tokens.
cards.flavor: "TWO!" — 20,000 people, on their feet, fingers in the air.
cards.art: bloodied babyface kicking out at the last instant, referee's hand slapping the mat, crowd erupting, classic wrestling arena

cards.name: You Better Call Somebody!
cards.rules: Whenever one or more creatures you control with power 4 or greater attack, create a Pop token.
cards.flavor: "The pyro hits, the crowd rises — somebody's about to go through a table."
cards.art: monstrous wrestler's pyro entrance, red lights and explosions, arena crowd on its feet, 1998 WWF

cards.name: Swanton Bomb
cards.rules:
Swanton Bomb deals 3 damage to target creature.
Create a Pop token.
cards.art: daredevil wrestler mid-swan dive off the top turnbuckle onto a prone opponent, crowd on its feet

cards.name: Ref, Do Your Job!
cards.rules:
Counter target spell that targets you or a permanent you control.
Create a Pop token.
cards.flavor: "The whole arena saw it — and now the ref has too."
cards.art: babyface wrestler pointing at the referee while the heel hides brass knuckles behind his back, crowd pointing and roaring, classic wrestling arena

cards.name: The Rock, People's Champion
cards.rules:
When The Rock enters the battlefield, create a Pop token.
{1}{R}, {T}, Sacrifice a Pop token: The Rock deals 3 damage to target creature. *(The People's Elbow.)*
cards.flavor: "If you smell... what The Rock... is cooking."
cards.art: the people's champion raising the eyebrow mid-ring, crowd exploding, 1999 WWF arena

cards.name: The Jobber
cards.rules:
{T}: Add one mana of any color.
Whenever you gain Momentum, untap The Jobber. This ability triggers only once each turn.
cards.art: jobber wrestler in plain trunks getting ready in a dim locker room, taping his wrists, knowing he's putting someone over tonight, 1990s WWF

cards.name: Cultivate
cards.rules: Search your library for up to two basic land cards, reveal those cards, put one onto the battlefield tapped and the other into your hand, then shuffle.
cards.flavor: "Everybody taps." *(invented — Stu stretching trainees, and the lands enter tapped)*
cards.art: dim basement gym with worn mats and exposed pipes, an old trainer stretching a young wrestler on the mat, framed photos of legends on the wall, Calgary

cards.name: Three Visits
cards.rules: Search your library for a Forest card, put that card onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.
cards.art: wrestler's-eye view of the endless touring road, arena marquee glowing at night in a small town, battered rental car, duffel bag, 1990s

cards.name: Rampant Growth
cards.rules: Search your library for a basic land card, put that card onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.
cards.art: 90s painted style, semi-realistic. A wrestler's physique swelling to impossible proportions mid-flex, shirt seams straining, veins roping his arms — a sly, knowing locker-room wink; an ajar gym bag with a vial just visible in the background. Suggestive, never explicit.

cards.name: Farseek
cards.rules: Search your library for a Plains, Island, Swamp, or Mountain card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.
cards.flavor: "Every main event starts as a date on a calendar." *(invented)*
cards.art: 90s painted style, semi-realistic. A booker's office wall covered in venue contracts and marked-up calendars, red circles around arena dates months out, coffee rings, cigarette smoke, 1990s

cards.name: Road Dogg, Jesse James
cards.rules:
Tag team with Billy Gunn, Mr. Ass *(At the beginning of your upkeep, if you control both members of one or more tag teams, create a Pop token. Only one token is created this way per turn.)*
Remove any number of Momentum from yourself. Add one mana of any color for every two Momentum removed this way. Activate only once each turn.
cards.art: 90s painted style, semi-realistic. Road Dogg on the mic mid-intro, one arm raised working a roaring late-90s WWF crowd into a frenzy, D-X glow behind him, 1998

cards.name: Cue the Pyro
cards.rules: Sacrifice any number of Pop tokens. Add {R}{R} for each token sacrificed this way.
cards.flavor: "When the pyro hits, the roof comes off." *(invented)*
cards.art: 90s painted style, semi-realistic. Massive entrance pyro erupting on the stage as a silhouetted wrestler poses on the ramp, sparks and smoke filling a 1999 WWF arena, crowd on its feet

cards.name: Cut a Promo
cards.rules:
Draw two cards.
Gain 1 Momentum.
cards.flavor: "_Grab the mic. Tell the truth. Watch the roof come off._" *(invented)*
cards.art: defiant wrestler standing on the turnbuckles holding a microphone high, roaring late-90s arena crowd with signs, Attitude Era WWF

cards.name: Mick Foley, Hardcore Legend
cards.rules: Whenever Mick Foley, Hardcore Legend is dealt damage, draw a card. This ability triggers only once each turn.
cards.flavor: "_He gets knocked down, and the whole arena holds its breath._" *(invented)*
cards.art: battered hardcore wrestler in flannel shirt grinning through a bloodied face, rising from a pile of broken tables, shocked roaring crowd, 1998 WWF

cards.name: Harmonize
cards.rules: Draw three cards.
cards.flavor: "_Catch your breath. The crowd isn't done with you yet._" *(invented)*
cards.art: exhausted wrestler on one knee in the middle of the ring, roaring crowd willing him back to his feet, 1998 WWF arena

cards.name: Jim Ross, Voice of the Attitude Era
cards.rules: {T}: Draw a card. Activate only if you gained Momentum this turn.
cards.flavor: "_This crowd is on its feet — and so is he!_" *(invented)*
cards.art: legendary wrestling announcer in a black cowboy hat calling a match at ringside, headset on, roaring 1998 WWF arena behind him

cards.name: Against All Odds
cards.rules: Draw two cards. If an opponent has more Momentum than you, draw three cards instead.
cards.art: bloodied underdog wrestler rising to his feet while the villain looks on in disbelief, crowd erupting, 1998 WWF arena

cards.name: Fight Forever
cards.rules: Discard your hand, then draw three cards.
cards.flavor: "_They chanted for one more. He gave them everything._" *(invented)*
cards.art: exhausted wrestler on his knees demanding the referee not stop the match, deafening roaring crowd with "fight forever" signs, 1998 WWF arena

cards.name: WWF Intercontinental Championship
cards.rules: {T}: Draw a card. Activate only if you have 5 or more Momentum.
cards.flavor: "_The workhorse title. Carry it, and the crowd carries you._" *(invented)*
cards.art: gleaming intercontinental championship belt raised high overhead by a silhouetted wrestler, adoring roaring crowd, 1998 WWF arena

cards.name: The Hot Tag
cards.rules: Untap target creature you control. It gets +2/+2 until end of turn. Draw a card.
cards.art: wrestler leaping off the ring apron to tag in their partner mid-match, crowd exploding to its feet, 1998 WWF arena

cards.name: Guardian Project
cards.rules: Whenever a nontoken creature you control enters, if it doesn't have the same name as another creature you control or a creature card in your graveyard, draw a card.
cards.flavor: "_Every name on the wall earned its spotlight._" *(invented)*
cards.art: gritty 1990s wrestling training school at dawn, trainees running the ropes and taking bumps in a converted warehouse, sweat and determination

cards.name: Collective Unconscious
cards.rules: Draw a card for each creature you control.
cards.art: entire arena crowd on its feet as one, a sea of signs and camera flashes, the building itself seeming to breathe — the crowd as a single mind, 1998 WWF

cards.name: Ringside Official
cards.rules: Whenever an opponent casts their first noncreature spell each turn, draw a card unless that player pays {X}, where X is this creature's power.
cards.art: veteran referee in a striped shirt sliding into position for the three-count, sternly admonishing a rule-breaking heel wrestler, 1998 WWF arena

cards.name: Stu Hart, Master of the Dungeon
cards.rules: Whenever another creature you control with power 2 or less enters, you may pay {1}. If you do, draw a card.
cards.flavor: "_In the Dungeon, you learned — or you limped._" *(invented)*
cards.art: grizzled old trainer Stu Hart watching over young wrestlers drilling on worn mats in a dim basement gym, single bare bulb overhead, sweat and grit, 1980s Calgary — the legendary Dungeon

cards.name: Judgment Day
cards.rules: Destroy all creatures.
cards.art: a heroic wrestler standing tall in the ring with arms raised as a gavel slams down in the foreground, defeated heels scattered around, confetti falling, 1998 WWF arena

cards.name: The Clean Finish
cards.rules: Exile target creature. Its controller gains life equal to its power.
cards.flavor: "_No chair. No ref bump. Just three._" *(invented)*
cards.art: a babyface wrestler pinning a heel clean in the center of the ring, referee's hand slapping the mat for three, crowd roaring approval, 1997 WWF arena

cards.name: The Clothesline
cards.rules: The Clothesline deals 3 damage to target creature. You gain 1 Momentum.
cards.art: a babyface wrestler delivering a massive running clothesline, the heel flipping backwards, crowd leaping to its feet, 1997 WWF arena

cards.name: The Spear
cards.rules:
Target creature you control deals damage equal to its power to target creature you don't control. If that creature is still on the battlefield, put a stun counter on it.
You gain 1 Momentum.
cards.art: a powerhouse babyface driving a spear into a heel, both suspended mid-impact, the heel's eyes rolled back, crowd erupting, 1998 arena

cards.name: The Zamboni Incident
cards.rules: The Zamboni Incident deals 5 damage to each creature. You gain 2 Momentum.
cards.art: Stone Cold Steve Austin driving a Zamboni down the entrance ramp straight toward the ring, wrestlers scattering, crowd losing its mind, 1998 WWF arena

cards.name: Pride Before the Fall
cards.rules: Each opponent chooses a creature they control. Destroy each creature you don't control that wasn't chosen this way. You gain 2 Momentum.
cards.flavor: "_He wanted it all. Now it's all he's got._" *(invented)*
cards.art: A heel champion standing alone in the middle of the ring, his fallen allies scattered around him, the babyface army standing tall and untouched on the entrance ramp, crowd roaring, late-90s arena

cards.name: Disqualification
cards.rules:
This spell costs {2} less to cast if it targets a tapped creature.
Exile target creature.
cards.art: A referee holding aloft a steel chair the heel just got caught swinging, the heel protesting with his hands up, the babyface getting his hand raised, late-90s arena

cards.name: Moment of Clarity
cards.rules: Gain control of target creature until end of turn. Untap it. It gains haste. You gain 1 Momentum.
cards.flavor: "_For one fight, he remembered who he was._" *(invented)*
cards.art: A heel wrestler lowering his steel chair, staring at his own reflection in the arena's big screen, the babyface crowd rising to its feet behind him, late-90s arena

cards.name: Clear the Ring
cards.rules: Destroy target artifact or enchantment.
cards.flavor: "_If it ain't nailed down, it's gone._" *(invented)*
cards.art: A babyface wrestler tossing a steel chair and a foreign object out of the ring over the top rope, the heel manager protesting at ringside, late-90s arena

cards.name: Shawn Michaels, The Showstopper
cards.rules:
*Sweet Chin Music* — When Shawn Michaels enters, it deals 4 damage to target creature.
Whenever Shawn Michaels attacks, create a Heat token.
cards.flavor: "_I'm just a sexy boy._" (his theme song — real)
cards.art: Shawn Michaels tuning up the band in the corner — stomping his foot, slapping his thigh, 1997 DX leather-chaps-and-heart-shades look, dazed opponent rising on wobbly legs mid-ring, roaring Attitude Era crowd

cards.name: Billy Gunn, Mr. Ass
cards.rules:
Tag team with Road Dogg, Jesse James *(At the beginning of your upkeep, if you control both members of one or more tag teams, create a Pop token. Only one token is created this way per turn.)*
When Billy Gunn enters, create a Heat token.
cards.flavor: "_I'm the one Billy Gunn, and I'm an ass man!_" (his song — real)
cards.art: 90s painted style, semi-realistic. Billy Gunn hitting the Fameasser — leaping leg drop onto a dazed opponent — Road Dogg going wild in the background, 1998 WWF DX gear, roaring Attitude Era crowd

cards.name: Sportatorium
cards.rules:
Sportatorium enters tapped unless you have no Momentum.
{T}: Add {W} or {R}.
cards.flavor: "_Von Erich country._" *(real — the Dallas Sportatorium was World Class's home)*
cards.art: The Dallas Sportatorium, 1980s — an old boxing arena, the Von Erichs' home turf, Texas wrestling at its most heroic

cards.name: Hart Dungeon
cards.rules:
Hart Dungeon enters tapped unless you have no Momentum.
{T}: Add {R} or {G}.
cards.flavor: "_Stu's basement. Where legends were stretched._" *(real — the Hart Dungeon in Calgary)*
cards.art: A basement training facility, 1980s Calgary — mats on concrete, Stu Hart stretching a student, the legendary Hart Dungeon

cards.name: VFW Hall
cards.rules:
VFW Hall enters tapped unless you have no Momentum.
{T}: Add {W} or {G}.
cards.flavor: "_Folding chairs. Low ceiling. The most honest wrestling there is._" *(invented)*
cards.art: A VFW hall indie show, 1998 — folding chairs around a ring, a low ceiling, the grassroots heart of wrestling

cards.name: Second Wind
cards.rules:
As an additional cost to cast this spell, remove 4 Momentum.
Target creature gains indestructible until end of turn. Untap it.
cards.art: a babyface wrestler kicking out at two, sitting bolt upright while the heel stares in disbelief — the crowd on its feet, 1998

cards.name: Rising Star
cards.rules: Remove 3 Momentum: Put two +1/+1 counters on Rising Star. Activate only as a sorcery.
cards.art: a young babyface wrestler in the ring, mid-match, shaking off a beating as the crowd rises — 1998, the moment the rookie becomes a star

cards.name: The Face Turn
cards.rules: Exile target creature. Destroy all other creatures. Return the exiled card to the battlefield under your control. It has haste.
cards.art: dramatic arena moment — a wrestler tearing away a black heel-faction shirt to reveal white and red beneath, sprinting down the entrance ramp toward a chaotic ring, crowd on its feet, flash photography, Attitude Era arena

cards.name: Scotty 2 Hotty, Too Cool
cards.rules:
When Scotty 2 Hotty enters the battlefield, behold another Wrestler. *(To behold another Wrestler, choose another Wrestler you control or reveal a Wrestler card from your hand.)*
If a Wrestler was beheld this way, Scotty 2 Hotty gains haste until end of turn.
cards.art: high-energy wrestler mid-dance-shimmy sprinting down the entrance ramp, crowd on its feet bouncing along, 1999 WWF arena, flash photography, pure Attitude Era joy

cards.name: No-Sell
cards.rules: Target creature you control gains indestructible until end of turn.
cards.art: heroic wrestler standing defiant through a cloud of dust and debris, arms spread, completely unmoved as a steel chair bounces off him, crowd roaring, Attitude Era arena

cards.name: Rope Break
cards.rules: {T}: Untap target attacking creature. Prevent all combat damage that would be dealt to and dealt by that creature this turn.
cards.flavor: "_The ref sees the ropes — clean break, now._" *(invented)*
cards.art: close-up of a wrestler's hand grabbing the bottom rope while the referee slides in calling for the break, the attacker forced to release, arena crowd leaning in, Attitude Era WWF

cards.name: Chris Jericho, Y2J
cards.rules: Whenever you sacrifice a Pop, untap Chris Jericho.
cards.art: high-energy wrestler with arms spread basking in a deafening crowd pop, lights blazing, long hair flying, 1999 WWF arena — the millennium man arriving

cards.name: Hollywood Hulk Hogan, nWo Leader
cards.rules:
When Hollywood Hulk Hogan enters the battlefield, each opponent loses 2 Momentum and you gain 2 Momentum.
Whenever Hollywood Hulk Hogan attacks, each opponent loses 1 Momentum and you gain 1 Momentum.
{2}{U}{B}, {T}: Gain control of target creature until end of turn. Untap it. It gains haste until end of turn.
cards.art: bleach-blond mustached giant in black nWo t-shirt, mocking the crowd with hand cupped to ear, spray-paint can in hand, dark 1996 WCW arena, black-and-white faction colors

cards.name: Hollywood Leg Drop
cards.rules:
As an additional cost to cast this spell, remove 9 Momentum.
Exile target creature. Its controller discards a card and loses 2 Momentum. You gain 2 Momentum.
cards.flavor: "_Cup the ear. Drop the leg. It's over, brother._"
cards.art: bleach-blond giant in black nWo shirt dropping a crushing leg across a fallen opponent's chest, mocking the booing crowd with the other hand, dark 1996 WCW arena

cards.name: The Rock, Corporate Champion
cards.rules:
When The Rock enters the battlefield, create a Heat token.
Whenever another creature enters the battlefield under your control, create a Heat token. Do this only once each turn. *(Everyone joins the Corporate parade.)*
{1}{B}, {T}, Sacrifice a Heat token: Target opponent discards a card.
cards.flavor: "Know your role, and shut your mouth!"
cards.art: smug corporate champion holding the title high, flanked by suits, crowd booing with thumbs down, 1998 WWF arena

cards.name: Paul Bearer, Keeper of the Urn
cards.rules:
Defender.
When Paul Bearer enters the battlefield, create a Heat token.
cards.art: pale ghostly mortician clutching a golden urn, high-voice shriek energy, crowd booing with thumbs down, 1997 WWF arena

cards.name: Edge, King of the Ring
cards.rules:
Whenever Edge attacks, create a Heat token.
Tag team with Christian, Edge's Brother *(At the beginning of your upkeep, if you control both members of one or more tag teams, create a Pop token. Only one token is created this way per turn.)*
cards.flavor: "You think you know me." *(his theme song — real)*
cards.art: arrogant newly-crowned King of the Ring in crown and robe, sneering at a booing crowd, 2001 WWF arena

cards.name: Christian, Edge's Brother
cards.rules:
When Christian enters the battlefield, create a Heat token.
Tag team with Edge, King of the Ring *(At the beginning of your upkeep, if you control both members of one or more tag teams, create a Pop token. Only one token is created this way per turn.)*
cards.flavor: "It's Edge AND Christian. Say both names." *(invented, approved by Wesley 2026-09-23)*
cards.art: bitter wrestler standing in another man's shadow, arms crossed, crowd ignoring him, 2001 WWF arena

cards.name: The Godfather, Ladies' Man
cards.rules: When The Godfather enters the battlefield, create two Heat tokens.
cards.art: flamboyant pimp-wrestler leading a conga line of dancers down the entrance ramp, crowd roaring with a mix of cheers and boos, 1998 WWF arena

cards.name: Eddie Guerrero, Latino Heat
cards.rules:
Whenever you activate an ability of Eddie Guerrero, create a Heat token.
Lie — Momentum costs you pay cost 1 less.
Cheat — {R}: Eddie Guerrero gets +2/+0 until end of turn.
Steal — {B}: Target opponent loses 1 Momentum and you gain 1 Momentum.
cards.flavor: "He's lying. He's cheating. He's stealing. He's winning." *(invented)*
cards.art: smug luchador leaning on the ropes, flicking a low blow behind the ref's back, crowd booing, 2000 WWF arena

cards.name: The Spanish Announce Table
cards.rules:
When The Spanish Announce Table enters the battlefield, create a Heat token.
{3}, {T}, Sacrifice The Spanish Announce Table: It deals 3 damage to target creature. Create two Heat tokens.
cards.flavor: "Somebody check on the Spanish announce team." *(invented)*
cards.art: shattered announce table at ringside, monitors sparking, a wrestler sprawled in the wreckage, crowd on its feet, 1998 WWF arena

cards.name: Crooked Ref
cards.rules: Whenever an opponent loses Momentum, create a Heat token. Do this only once each turn.
cards.art: sleazy referee with a wad of cash in his pocket, mid fast-count, heel wrestler grinning behind him, furious crowd, 1998 arena

cards.name: Get the Tables!
cards.rules:
Search your library for an Equipment card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle.
Create a Heat token.
cards.flavor: "D-VON! GET THE TABLES!" *(the Dudleyz' catchphrase — real)*
cards.art: D-Von sliding a table into the ring while Bubba Ray holds an opponent up, crowd roaring, 2000 WWF arena

cards.name: Ted DiBiase, The Million Dollar Man
cards.rules: Remove 2 Momentum from target opponent: Add one mana of any color. Activate only once each turn.
cards.art: A smug man in an expensive suit stuffing a wad of cash into a wrestler's trunks while the crowd boos; dollar signs worked into the background.

cards.name: Cheap Heat
cards.rules: Sacrifice any number of Heat tokens. Add {B} or {R} for each token sacrificed this way.
cards.flavor: "_Boo all you want — you're still watching._" *(invented)*
cards.art: A heel wrestler cupping his ear to a jeering crowd, smirking; the boos rendered as visible red sound waves he seems to be drinking in.

cards.name: The Production Truck
cards.rules:
{T}: Add {B} or {R}.
{T}, Sacrifice a creature: Target opponent loses 1 Momentum and you gain 1 Momentum.
cards.art: A massive TV production truck parked backstage at night, satellite dish up, glowing monitors visible through the open back; a silhouetted figure at the mixing board like a puppet master.

cards.name: Backstage Ambush
cards.rules: {T}: Add {C}. {T}: Add {U} or {B}. Activate this ability only if an opponent lost Momentum this turn.
cards.art: A dim backstage hallway — two silhouettes jumping a third from behind a stack of equipment crates; a single overhead bulb swinging.

cards.name: Take the Fall
cards.rules: As an additional cost to cast this spell, sacrifice a creature. Add {B}{B}{B}.
cards.flavor: "_Somebody's taking the pin, and it ain't me._" *(invented)*
cards.art: A heel wrestler shoving a smaller wrestler into the path of a charging opponent, diving clear at the last second.

cards.name: Paying Dues
cards.rules: At the beginning of your upkeep, you draw a card and you lose 1 life.
cards.flavor: "_Power is never given. It's taken — one favor at a time._" *(invented)*
cards.art: sinister promoter in a dark backstage office sliding a contract across a desk, stacks of cash and a title belt in the shadows, 1998 WCW

cards.name: Steal the Spotlight
cards.rules:
Target opponent loses 2 Momentum.
Draw two cards.
cards.art: cocky heel wrestler snatching a microphone from a fallen opponent, crowd booing with thumbs down, 1998 WCW arena

cards.name: Bobby Heenan, The Brain
cards.rules: {T}: Draw a card. Activate only if an opponent lost Momentum this turn.
cards.flavor: "_I speak for the winners. The losers can get their own manager._" *(invented)*
cards.art: smug weasel-faced manager in a loud 1990s blazer, leaning on the broadcast desk with a headset around his neck, pointing and laughing at a fallen wrestler, 1996 WCW arena

cards.name: Mind Games
cards.rules: Draw X cards. Each opponent loses 1 Momentum for each card drawn this way.
cards.flavor: "_The match is won before the bell rings._" *(invented)*
cards.art: scheming nWo manager whispering into a wrestler's ear in a dark backstage hallway, glowing monitors and scattered contracts, 1998 WCW

cards.name: Work the Crowd
cards.rules: Target opponent loses 1 Momentum. Draw a card.
cards.flavor: "_They paid to boo. Give them their money's worth._" *(invented)*
cards.art: cocky nWo heel on the turnbuckle cupping his ear, taunting a furious booing crowd, 1997 WCW arena

cards.name: Outside Interference
cards.rules: Return target creature card from your graveyard to your hand. Target opponent loses 1 Momentum.
cards.art: hooded nWo wrestler sliding into the ring under the bottom rope while the referee's back is turned, crowd erupting, 1998 WCW arena

cards.name: Tale of the Tape
cards.rules: Draw two cards. Scry 1 if an opponent lost Momentum this turn.
cards.flavor: "_He's studied every match. He knows what's coming._" *(invented)*
cards.art: heel wrestler in a dark locker room studying a wall of CRT monitors showing his opponent's matches, circling weaknesses with a marker, 1998 WCW

cards.name: Paul Heyman, The Mad Scientist
cards.rules: Whenever you sacrifice a Heat, you may pay {1}. If you do, draw a card.
cards.flavor: "_Chaos is just opportunity with better lighting._" *(invented)*
cards.art: Paul Heyman in an ECW arena, 1997 — cell phone to his ear, other hand gesturing wildly at the chaos in the ring, grin of a man whose plan is working

cards.name: The Swerve
cards.rules: Each player discards their hand, then draws seven cards. Each opponent loses 2 Momentum.
cards.flavor: "_Nobody saw it coming. That was the point._" *(invented)*
cards.art: the shocking betrayal mid-match — a tag partner turning on their own partner with a steel chair, crowd stunned silent, 1998 WCW arena

cards.name: Backstage Politics
cards.rules: Search your library for a card, put it into your hand, then shuffle. You lose 2 Momentum.
cards.art: heel wrestler shaking hands with a suited executive in a backstage office, contracts on the desk, 1998 WCW — the deal behind the deal

cards.name: The Writers' Room
cards.rules:
{T}: Add {C}.
{B}, {T}, Sacrifice The Writers' Room, Sacrifice a creature: Draw a card, then discard a card.
cards.art: the WWF writers' room, 1999 — a whiteboard covered in crossed-out names, cigarette smoke, Vince Russo pacing with a coffee

cards.name: Cheap Shot
cards.rules: Target creature gets -2/-2 until end of turn. Its controller loses 1 Momentum.
cards.art: heel wrestler delivering a low blow behind the referee's back while the ref's distracted, 1997 ECW crowd howling

cards.name: Bag of Tacks
cards.rules: Bag of Tacks deals 4 damage to target creature. Its controller loses 1 Momentum.
cards.flavor: "_He knew exactly where the bump was landing._" *(invented)*
cards.art: heel wrestler pouring a bag of thumbtacks onto the mat mid-match, crowd wincing, 1998 WWF arena — the premeditated spot

cards.name: You're Outta Here!
cards.rules: Return target creature to its owner's hand. Its controller loses 2 Momentum.
cards.art: the referee center-frame doing the dramatic point toward the backstage area, a random heel wrestler looking genuinely appalled that the ref would dare send them away, 1998 WWF arena

cards.name: Future Endeavors
cards.rules: Target opponent sacrifices a creature. Create a Heat token.
cards.flavor: "_We wish them well._" *(invented; homage to WWE's infamous release announcement)*
cards.art: wrestler carrying a cardboard box of belongings out of the arena backstage, head down, road cases stacked around them, 1999 WWF — the walkout after the release

cards.name: Buried
cards.rules: Destroy target creature.
cards.flavor: "_The office decided the push was over._" *(invented)*

bible_markdown:
# WWE × Magic: The Gathering — Monday Night Wars

**Project Bible version:** 0.3 (updated 2026-09-25: audit resolutions — Cultivate/Farseek restored, Get the Tables! v0.2, BF-009 duplicate resolved; commanders marked locked)
**Status:** 🟢 Active — this file is the single source of truth
**Working title:** WWE × Magic: The Gathering — Monday Night Wars

---

## 1. Project Overview

A custom Magic: The Gathering design project inspired by professional
wrestling during the Attitude Era and Monday Night Wars (1996–2001).

The goal is not simply to place wrestler names and images onto Magic cards.
The goal is to create a **serious, playable Magic product that feels
unmistakably like professional wrestling** — translating recognizable
wrestling concepts, personalities, factions, rivalries, match experiences,
and storytelling into mechanically coherent Magic cards and gameplay.

## 2. Initial Product

Two Commander decks, designed as a playable pair:

- **Babyface deck** — primarily babyface-aligned. Locked commander:
  **Stone Cold Steve Austin** (W/R/G — Naya). Theme: *The Comeback*.
- **Heel deck** — primarily heel-aligned. Locked commander:
  **Hollywood Hulk Hogan** (U/B/R). Theme: *Control the Show*.

Each deck also gets a **30-card sideboard** of spare cards for swapping
between games (not an in-game Commander sideboard — Commander has no
sideboard rule).

The two Commander decks are the priority. A larger WWE-themed set may be
developed later, but the full set is **not** the immediate design target.

## 3. Historical Scope

- **Primary era:** approximately **1996–2001** — the Monday Night Wars,
  the Attitude Era, the WWF vs. WCW rivalry. The era restriction governs
  the wrestling portrayals and events depicted on cards.
- **Promotions:** WWF/WWE and WCW are both permitted. Per the project
  owner, **ECW is also fair game**.

## 4. Design Goals

### 4.1 Playability
Cards must function as real Magic cards. Respect established design
principles: mana costs, color pie, card advantage, tempo, creature sizing,
removal, combat, rarity, complexity, and Commander gameplay. Cards should
not receive excessive power simply because a wrestler is famous.

### 4.2 Wrestling Identity
Wrestling concept → Magic gameplay concept. Examples:

- Building crowd support → building Momentum
- Getting beaten down → losing life / losing permanents / being under pressure
- Surviving a beating → resilience / surviving combat
- Comeback → gaining advantages after falling behind
- Tag team → coordinated creature mechanics
- Faction → groups of mechanically related cards
- Championship → Equipment or other permanent representing a title
- Match → enchantment / Saga / battlefield condition
- Signature move → activated or triggered ability
- Finisher → powerful payoff that requires setup
- Interference → manipulation of combat or other players
- Betrayal → sacrificing or turning against an ally
- Heel tactics → stealing, manipulating, exploiting, or disrupting opponents

## 5. Design Philosophy

**Magic first, wrestling second — but both must matter.** A card should
work as a Magic card even if the player doesn't know the reference, while
wrestling fans recognize what it represents. Communicate wrestling through
mechanics, flavor, naming, card types, art direction, gameplay patterns,
factions, and storytelling.

**Avoid "100 famous wrestlers."** Every important Superstar needs a
**mechanical identity** — persona, role in the era, signature behavior,
faction, relationships, storyline function, in-ring identity.

**Mechanics must reinforce themes.** A mechanic should create interesting
gameplay, support the deck's identity, feel like wrestling, be
understandable, have enough design space, and work within Magic's rules.
**Favor a small number of deep mechanics over a large number of shallow ones.**

## 6. Decision Status System

- 🟢 **LOCKED** — formally established; do not change without revisiting.
- 🔵 **APPROVED / PROVISIONAL** — preferred direction; can evolve through
  testing or discussion.
- 🟡 **UNDER DISCUSSION** — unresolved design question.
- 🟠 **PROTOTYPE** — being tested; not final.
- 🔴 **REJECTED** — deliberately removed; may be revisited with new info.

Full log: `design/decisions.md`.

## 7. Core Mechanic — Momentum 🟢 LOCKED

**Momentum** is a player resource representing crowd energy, match momentum,
and the emotional buildup toward a comeback or finishing sequence.

- Tracked as a number per player (not counters on a permanent).
- Players can gain, spend, check (thresholds), or lose Momentum.
- Persists until spent or removed; no inherent maximum.
- **Floor at zero (locked 2026-09-28):** Momentum can't go below 0 —
  removal beyond a player's total removes what's there. Rulings (Heat
  token's gain is independent of the loss; DiBiase-style removal costs
  must be fully payable): `design/momentum.md`.
- Three utilization categories (🔵 provisional): **Spend** (pay for
  abilities/bonuses), **Check** (threshold effects without spending),
  **Require** (Momentum as an additional casting cost — finishers live here).
- Conceptual thresholds: 5 and 10 Momentum (balance TBD in playtesting).

**Babyfaces: generate → build → protect → capitalize.** Earned through
combat, resilience, teamwork, crowd support, and comebacks. Deck fantasy:
*"You can beat me down, but you can't keep me down."*

**Heels: manipulate → steal → exploit → disrupt.** The lie/cheat/steal
identity — scheming (Lie), interference and cheap tricks (Cheat), draining
opponents' Momentum for their own benefit (Steal).

Full spec: `design/momentum.md`.

### Signature Token — Pop 🟢 LOCKED

**Pop** is a Token Artifact printed as an insert with the Babyface deck (not a
main-deck slot). Card file: `cards/colorless/SET-001-pop.md`.

- "{1}, {T}, Sacrifice this token: Gain 2 Momentum."
- "{T}, Sacrifice this token: Target creature gets +2/+2 until end of turn."

The crowd's eruption made tangible: bank it (pay {1}, fuel the Momentum
engine toward finisher thresholds) or crack it free in combat (the
immediate rally — "get the guy back in it"). Because it's an artifact,
opponents can destroy banked Pops — counterplay that raw Momentum doesn't
offer. Generator designs to follow; balance rules: never a free Pop, the
{1} on banking is load-bearing, both decks keep artifact removal.

### Signature Token — Heat 🟢 LOCKED

**Heat** is a Token Artifact printed as an insert with the Heel deck (not a
main-deck slot). Card file: `cards/colorless/SET-002-heat.md`. The heel
mirror of Pop — same sackable, modal, Clue/Treasure-style structure,
completely different job.

- "{1}, {T}, Sacrifice this token: Target opponent loses 1 Momentum and you gain 1 Momentum."
- "{T}, Sacrifice this token: Draw a card, then discard a card."

The face banks cheers; the heel siphons boos (same {1} cost, same 2-point
Momentum swing, different distribution) and schemes (free loot vs Pop's free
combat trick). Design principle: Momentum is fair game, life totals aren't.
Stealing Pops was considered and rejected. Same generator gating rules as Pop;
watch loot smoothing in Grixis during playtesting.

### Finisher Framework 🟢 LOCKED

**Finisher** is a formal instant/sorcery subtype (like Trap or Lesson).

- Finishers are **sorceries** by default — earned, telegraphed, interactable.
- **Commander asymmetry:** Hollywood Hulk Hogan's finisher is a sorcery
  (the leg drop: cup the ear, crowd counts, then it lands); Stone Cold
  Steve Austin's is an **instant** (the Stunner came out of nowhere).
- **Casting cost: spend Momentum** — "As an additional cost to cast this
  spell, remove N Momentum": **9 for sorcery finishers, 10 for instants**
  (the instant premium — flexibility costs more). Spending the tank is the
  story: everything in the building went into one move.
- Not every wrestler gets a finisher. Drawing yours should feel like
  a moment.
- The subtype unlocks finisher tutors, discounts, and "whenever you cast
  a Finisher" triggers.
- **Locked vs. open:** the subtype, sorcery-by-default/instant-exception,
  and the 9/10 Momentum additional costs are locked. The exact
  comprehensive-rules wording is open (see Open Questions).

### Tag Team 🟢 LOCKED

Coordinated wrestling teams. **Rule (locked 2026-09-23; amended 2026-09-28):** cards with
"Tag team with [Name]" are paired. At the beginning of your upkeep, if you
control both members of one or more tag teams, create a Pop token — only one token per turn, no matter
how many completed teams you control. (The 9/23 version gave heel tag teams Heat instead; Wesley
reworked it 9/28: the hot tag always pops.) Implemented as a set-level rule (like
the monarch), not per-card triggers. Full spec: `design/mechanics.md`.

## 10. Card & Deck Design Standards

**Every significant card** must answer: Is the mana cost / color pie /
power level right? Is it doing too many things? Does it create interesting
decisions? Is its role clear? What does it do early, late, ahead, behind?
Does the mechanic communicate the wrestling concept? Is it era-authentic?
Does it belong in this deck?

**Power target:** casual Commander bracket 2 — splashy and fun, never
competitive-level. The bracket-2 bar applies to every card review.

**Decks** must be cohesive experiences: clear commander identity, primary
strategy, subthemes, ramp, card draw, interaction, board presence,
finishers, functional mana base, coherent curve — playable against each
other while feeling substantially different.

## 11. Workflow

1. **Foundation** — goals, product, scope, commanders, themes, core mechanics
2. **Mechanical architecture** — colors, Momentum rules, tokens, finishers,
   matches, factions, tag teams
3. **Commander design** — Austin, Hogan, alternates
4. **Deck skeletons** — counts and curves before individual cards
5. **Roster** — who's in, deck, color identity, faction, mechanical identity
6. **Card design** — systematic, with IDs and versions
7. **Playtesting** — goldfish, then babyface vs. heel
8. **Refinement** — costs, quantities, thresholds, power
9. **Finalization** — templating, color, history, names, flavor, art, lists

## 12. Research Standards

- **Magic research:** reputable design/rules sources; corroborate important
  claims (skeletons, curves, color pie, rates, Commander design, templating).
- **WWE historical research:** verify historical claims with reputable
  sources — wrestlers, factions, championships, storylines, matches,
  signature moves, timelines. Accuracy matters for cards based on real events.
